about: Expression grammar conformance table. Each case parses `src` as one Puzzle template expression with github.com/magic-spells/puzzle/packages/puzzle-lang/expr (Parse), its first byte at `base` (default line 1, column 1, offset 0). An ok case expects the tree printed by expr.Print and the node positions printed by expr.PrintPositions: every node's start as line:col:offset, in Walk order. expr.Print is a compact S-expression: literals print as values (numbers as JavaScript prints them, strings single-quoted); a name prints bare; (tpl …) is a template literal, alternating text segments and substitutions; (. a b) (?. a b) ([] a i) (?.[] a i) are member reads; (call callee args…) a call; (global Math.round) and (global Number) the allowed JavaScript globals; (=> (params) body) an arrow function; (op a b) a unary, binary, or logical operator; (? test then else) a conditional; (array …) and (object (key value) … (shorthand)) literals; and (chain …) the extent of an optional chain. A failing case expects the exact error message at the exact line, column, and offset. Columns count bytes, and only LF starts a new line. Options: `argument: true` parses the source as a call argument (the template parser's formatter arguments), where an arrow function is legal at the top level; `handler: true` parses an @event handler value (PuzzleKit only), where `event` is the DOM event and a chain rooted at it is unrestricted; `bindings` lists the names enclosing template constructs bind, which read as values and can never be called. Both hosts run this file: PuzzleKit through this module's tests, Sites by importing the module at its tag.
